dev_kfree_skb.reason: skb release helper is exposed as a macro and should not leak macro expansion into Rust

dev_lstats_add.reason: per-cpu stats helper; bindgen cannot cross the inline boundary directly
dev_lstats_add.signature: void rust_helper_dev_lstats_add(struct net_device *dev, unsigned int len)

netdev_priv.reason: private data access helper; Rust side should not depend on C macro expansion

direct_ffi_candidates.dev_lstats_read: regular function used by stats callback
direct_ffi_candidates.rtnl_link_register: regular exported rtnl link registration function
direct_ffi_candidates.rtnl_link_unregister: regular exported rtnl link unregistration function

linux/kernel.h.reason: The Rust side should avoid depending on generic C helper macros from `linux/kernel.h`.

linux/module.h.reason: Use `kernel::ThisModule`/`module!` instead of bindgen exposure for `THIS_MODULE` and module lifecycle macros.

rtnl.reason: Link-type drivers need Rust-side rtnl registration and callback bridging.
required_surface: A typed link-ops description carrying `kind`, `priv_size`, `setup`, and optional `validate`.
Callback shims that keep raw `nlattr`/`netlink_ext_ack` handling out of driver code.

netdevice.reason: Link-type drivers configure `net_device` state, netdev ops, and setup flags.
required_surface: A typed `net_device` wrapper for `setup` field writes and private storage access.
A `net_device_ops`-style trait covering `open`, `stop`, and an ownership-safe `start_xmit` surface.
Enough constants/enums to set device type, flags, priv_flags, free-on-destroy policy, and MTU bounds.

stats.reason: Link-type drivers typically use lstats helpers and/or stats callbacks.
required_surface: Expose the per-cpu stats configuration constant for `setup` if the profile keeps that field write.
Provide a helper-backed `dev_lstats_add` wrapper that driver code can call without touching helper FFI directly.

skbuff.reason: Link-type drivers often consume skb objects in the xmit path.
required_surface: A move-only skb owner for `ndo_start_xmit` that frees on drop and can hand ownership back to the core on `NETDEV_TX_BUSY`.

body_plan: Keep this callback out of the first Rust loop until the corresponding abstraction and oracle evidence are ready.
